ideas.title: What I charge and why
ideas.thumbnailIdea: Plain background, one number set large, no face.
hooks: Everyone asks what I charge. Here is the actual number.
I'll tell you my exact pricing in 30 seconds.
ideas.script:
## Cold open
I get asked this every single week, so here it is.

## The numbers
- Setup fee covers discovery and the first build
- Retainer covers upkeep, monitoring and changes
- Nothing is hidden behind a call

## Close
That is the whole thing. No packages, no tiers.

inspiration.note: Number on screen in the first second — steal that opening

shotIdeas: Cutaway to the invoice on screen
Close-up on the number being written down
ideas.caption: Pricing, in the open. Setup, retainer, and what each one actually buys you.
ideas.notes: Keep it under 90 seconds. The number is the hook — do not bury it.

ideas.title: Why most automations fail in month two
hooks: Your automation did not break. Nobody owned it.
ideas.script:
## Cold open
Month one always works. Month two is where it goes quiet.

## Why
- The person who asked for it moved on
- Nobody watches the failure emails
- One upstream field gets renamed

## What to do instead
Give every workflow an owner and somewhere its failures are visible.
shotIdeas: Screen recording of a failed run
ideas.caption: Month one always works. Here is what happens in month two.

ideas.title: The first hire nobody tells you to make
titleOptions: The first hire that actually mattered
ideas.script:
## Cold open
Everyone said hire sales. I hired an operator instead.

## Why it worked
- Delivery stopped being the bottleneck
- I got my evenings back
- Sales got easier once delivery was boring
ideas.caption: Everyone said hire sales first. Here is what I did instead.
ideas.performanceNote: 12.4k views, best retention of the month. The 'it was not a salesperson' line is doing the work — reuse that shape.
